tasks.title: Embed many texts in few requests
tasks.description:
Implement `embed(texts, client)` in `src/embed.ts`. It returns `Promise<number[][]>`: one vector per text, in the same order as `texts`.

- Call `client.embeddings.create({ model: EMBED_MODEL, input })` where `input` is an array of texts.
- Send several texts per request, at most `MAX_BATCH` (16) in each. 40 texts take 3 requests.
- Every item in `res.data` has an `index` saying which input it belongs to. Put each vector at that position; do not rely on the order of `data`.
- `embed([])` returns `[]` without any request.

Keep the optional `client` parameter. The check watches the requests you send, and also replays a response whose items arrive in reverse order.
nextSteps: Run `node src/demo.ts` and read the error for embed.
Send all texts in one request and return the vectors.
Wrap the request in a loop over slices of at most MAX_BATCH texts.
Use each item's index to put its vector in the right place.
hints: Print `res.data[0]` once to see what an embedding item holds besides the numbers.
Slicing texts from `start` to `start + MAX_BATCH` gives one batch. The loop moves start forward by MAX_BATCH.
An item with index i in the batch that began at start belongs at position start + i of the result.

tasks.title: Cosine similarity by hand
tasks.description:
Implement `cosine(a, b)` in `src/embed.ts` without any library.

- Return the dot product of `a` and `b` divided by the length of `a` times the length of `b` (length = square root of the sum of squares).
- Return `0` when either vector is all zeros.
- Throw an `Error` when the two vectors have different lengths.

The check tries vectors pointing the same way, at right angles, opposite ways, of different lengths, and a zero vector.
nextSteps: Check the two lengths match before anything else.
Compute the dot product and both squared lengths in one loop.
Handle the zero vector, then divide.
hints: The local model already scales its vectors to length 1, so a dot product alone looks right in the demo. The check also uses vectors that are not length 1.
Three running sums are enough: a times b, a times a, and b times b.
If either squared length is 0, the answer is 0. Otherwise divide the dot product by the square root of the two squared lengths multiplied together.

tasks.title: Rank texts by meaning
tasks.description:
Implement `rank(query, texts, client)` in `src/embed.ts`. It returns `{ text, score }[]`:

- `score` is `cosine` of the query's vector and the text's vector.
- One result per text, sorted from the highest score to the lowest.
- Embed the query and all the texts with a single call to `embed` (one request for up to 15 texts).

The check ranks every handbook article for a question about dogs, counts the requests, and type-checks `src/embed.ts`.
nextSteps: Embed the query together with the texts in one call.
Score each text against the query vector.
Sort the results and run the demo.
hints: Put the query first in the list you send to embed, so its vector is easy to find.
Array destructuring can split the first vector from the rest in one line.
Map each text to { text, score: cosine(queryVector, vectors[i]) }, then sort by score, highest first.
